habitat: Flocks in lowland and riverine forest, lowveld broad-leaved woodland and thickets, and in coastal bush and dune forest.
summary: A locally common resident. Blacker than Helmeted Guineafowl, with black head-plumes, an unmarked black neck, a pale bill, pale outer secondaries and red eyes. The immature is barred chestnut, buff and black on the upper parts. The alarm is a rattle, and the breeding call is tick-tack, ticktack-tirr-tirr-tirr. Newman’s page uses the name Guttera pucherani. The stored name Guttera edouardi was left unchanged. The Kemp paper name Crested Guineafowl and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Helmeted Guineafowl has a blue neck, a red cap and a horny casque. Southern Crested Guineafowl is blacker, with black head-plumes and an unmarked black neck.

calls.description: A rattling alarm. When breeding, tick-tack, ticktack-tirr-tirr-tirr. Grade A alarm call from St Lucia, catalogued as Guttera pucherani, the name on Newman’s page. The filename is XC237779-1062_cut.mp3, so the file is marked as a cut.
